observations: A large black-outlined spiral eye dominates the upper center, its white iris coiling inward against a black field, with a yellow arc above and a row of red-filled oval shapes below it.
The right edge is bounded by a thick yellow zigzag line running the full height; the left side carries a yellow rectangular outline enclosing a bold magenta curved stroke.
A wide rectangular mouth zone in the lower third is filled with white block shapes outlined in red and dark brown, against a sky-blue ground that extends across the whole composition.
reading: One large spiral eye pulls attention to the center while the rest of the face spreads outward in competing zones of yellow, magenta, and sky blue. The zigzag right border acts as both edge and feature, giving the face an uneven, charged boundary. The mouth's white blocks feel blunt and frontal — somewhere between a grin and a grimace. The overall mood is loud and unsettled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #78 and #80, and title order matches recorded creation order for these three owned works. Where #78 builds its face from dark masses on teal, #79 opens into bright sky blue with a single dominant eye.

connections.reason: Both works place a wide rectangular mouth zone with white interior shapes low in the composition, but #78 builds its face from dark masses on teal while #79 opens the same structure onto bright sky blue with a single large spiral eye.

Both use saturated yellow as a dominant border or ground color and place a rectangular tooth-filled mouth low in the composition, though nnotb #154 scatters its forms loosely while #79 stacks its features in a tighter vertical column.

lookingQuestion: The zigzag line runs the full height of the right edge — does it read to you as a frame containing the face, or as part of the face itself?
ambiguities: The row of red-filled oval shapes between the eye and mouth could be read as teeth, a nose bridge, or a decorative band; no supplied metadata resolves this.
Candidate #80 shows a rounded, softer composition with no strong formal echo of the spiral eye or zigzag border and was not selected despite title adjacency.
